scope: The user-supplied 62-page textbook defines scope. No assertion of a separate official Gaza cancellation list.
reviewMethod: All 86 PDF pages were rendered and visually opened by assigned reviewers, including answer keys. Crops preserve original pixels using lossless WebP; handwritten answers and unreadable figures are not reconstructed.
limits: The collection is first-semester mock papers from several directorates, not a Gaza final-exam blueprint.
No OSI questions occur in the supplied exam collection; those exercises come from the textbook.
Only selected in-scope question items enter the active course; repeated and out-of-book material remains in the unchanged source PDF.
Written responses and diagrams use self-review, not automated grading.

SQL GROUP BY/HAVING, aggregate functions other than COUNT, and subquery exercises beyond the supplied book
CREATE/DROP/GRANT/REVOKE syntax exercises; DDL/DCL definitions remain in scope

answerKeyNotes: PDF pp4–5 reverse the descriptions under `get global root` and `set global root to`. Correct: get reads, set assigns. Do not reproduce the printed key as authoritative.
PDF p5 prints `DDL – Data Control Language` in an answer caption. The question correctly asks DCL. Imported comparison explicitly flags the typo.
PDF pp6,13,35 describe cascading updates/deletes as inherent to referential integrity. Integrity prevents orphan references; cascades require their own enabled options.
PDF p7 Q5/d2 key uses `project_tbl` although table is `project`, and `<=1500` although prompt says less than 1500. Corrected solution and exact conflict recorded in selected entry.
PDF p7 Q5/d3 key selects `proj_no` although names `proj_name` are requested, and uses `>=` instead of `>`. Corrected and visibly identified in selected entry.
PDF p9 quoted-value MCQ contains malformed `SELECT FROM ...` without a projection. Original stem retained, and limitation disclosed; item assesses quoted value type only.
PDF p14 employee/department key omits one source table from FROM and leaves common field Dep_no unqualified. Do not use its text as a model answer.

PDF p15 says there cannot be a database table without a primary key. A primary key is essential to the relational design expected here, but Access can store a table without one; avoid universal software claim.

PDF p16 claims INSERT fails because no primary-key value is supplied, but the prompt declares neither table schema nor whether the key is AutoNumber. Not enough context for a uniquely justified error; no question imported.
PDF p36 supplies alternative incomplete joins for a three-table query. A correct query needs both relationships together.

Phone security and memory keys use historical simplifications. App-store checks do not guarantee immunity to viruses, and iOS does free memory. Do not expand these claims into current technical guarantees.
delivery: Runtime crops preserve their original dimensions; selected files are compressed after visual/error-bound checks. originalSha256 records the archived original when encoding changes.
